clue.text: Substitute which may be turned…

definitions.meaning: to substitute one thing for another is to swap or exchange them
an electrical control you turn to work a light

explanation.surface: A replacement that can be rotated, leading into the next clue's phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into 4 across: such a control may be turned off and on.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap one thing for another is to make a change; a light control is also turned by hand.

clue.text: In a lot of people pains occur in this, the main trunk

definitions.text: In a lot of people pains occur in this, the main trunk

parts.words: In a lot of people pains occur in this, the main trunk
parts.note: the torso is where many people feel pain and is the body's main trunk; the main is also the sea, and a trunk is a box

explanation.surface: Many people get pains in their torso, the body's central trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old word for the sea, and a trunk is a storage box: a sailor's box.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor's storage box; the torso half also names where pains are felt.

clue.text: Soul of an athlete who keeps to the rails

definitions.text: an athlete who keeps to the rails
definitions.meaning: a runner who stays on the inside track

explanation.surface: The spirit of a runner who hugs the inside rail.
explanation.definitionFit: The inward spiritual self; also, playfully, a runner on the inside lane.

clue.text: Covered 1840 years ago

parts.note: at the time of the puzzle, 1840 years earlier was the year 150 CE; CL is Roman 150
AD marks a year of the Christian era

explanation.surface: Something concealed back in the second century.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared around 1990, so the date reached is the second century; Roman numerals then give the number.
explanation.definitionFit: Clad means dressed or clothed, a synonym for covered.

clue.text: … now and again

parts.note: read with the previous clue, a light control is turned this way, and the phrase also means occasionally

explanation.surface: The tail of the previous clue: something turned at intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for intermittently or occasionally.

clue.text: La veuve takes in the north outlook on the garden

indicators.note: takes in means one piece swallows the other

parts.note: la veuve is French for the widow
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A French widow welcomes the north to a garden view.
explanation.definitionFit: A glazed double door opening onto a garden gives a view of it.

clue.text: First class railway, but not at all stuffy

parts.note: A1 means first class, read as AI

explanation.surface: A top-class train that is pleasantly ventilated.
explanation.definitionFit: Well ventilated and fresh rooms are breezy, the opposite of stuffy.

clue.text: Old copper ripped off in a car?

parts.note: d stood for the old penny, a copper coin in pre-decimal British money
riven means torn apart

explanation.surface: A former policeman robbed while in his car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer; it is the old copper penny, abbreviated d. 'off' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being chauffeured in a car means being conveyed by a motorist.

clue.text: The foreign minstrel is apparently vexed by personal enquiries!

definitions.text: The foreign minstrel is apparently vexed by personal enquiries!

parts.words: The foreign minstrel is apparently vexed by personal enquiries!
parts.note: split as a foreigner's broken English, a singer refusing to perform; also, prying into private matters

explanation.surface: A visiting singer is annoyed by nosy questions.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NO SING, what a foreign minstrel might say in broken English; whole, it means prying.
explanation.definitionFit: Prying into other people's business is snooping.

clue.text: Sort of bloomer that's printed once a year

definitions.meaning: a plant that flowers and dies within one year

explanation.surface: A flower and a yearly publication, set side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant living one season and a yearbook both share the word for yearly.

clue.text: Almost a hit with the girl

parts.note: with in the sense of close beside or close to
Miss is the title of an unmarried girl

explanation.surface: Nearly scoring a success with a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot that narrowly fails to strike its target is an idiom for almost hitting.

clue.text: Indicate where one can see a cross-country race

definitions.meaning: to gesture at a spot so others look there
a horse race across country between markers

explanation.surface: Showing someone where to watch a steeplechase.
explanation.definitionFit: Gesturing at a location; also an amateur steeplechase between landmarks.

clue.text: It sounds like higher rent

indicators.note: the clue openly says the word that follows is matched by its sound

parts.note: the comparative of high, said aloud

explanation.surface: A rise in rent, sounding like a complaint about cost.
explanation.definitionFit: To rent something is to pay for its temporary use, a synonym.

clue.text: Get your hands on a small loan

definitions.meaning: to make contact with the fingers
slang for getting money from someone, as in putting the bite on a friend

explanation.surface: Grabbing a little borrowed money.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel with the fingers; also old slang for successfully borrowing cash.

clue.text: Adapt to food of a new form

indicators.note: a new form of the letters means they are put in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Getting used to eating something in an unfamiliar shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Weaning accustoms an infant to solid food instead of milk.

clue.text: Plus an unknown number of the antelope family

parts.note: to add is to plus
an is the indefinite article, A
X is the algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Adding an unknown number to a herd of antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition stands for 'a member of the antelope family'.
explanation.definitionFit: A North African desert antelope with spiral horns, so a member by example.

clue.text: Quarter pints of mushrooms contain hundreds of them

definitions.meaning: a gill is a measure of a quarter of a pint
the thin plates under a mushroom cap

explanation.surface: Small measures of mushroom soup with many pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An old liquid measure; also the radiating plates beneath a fungus cap.

clue.text: Those who do also serve as a queue

definitions.text: Those who do also serve as a queue

parts.words: Those who do also serve as a queue
parts.note: echoes Milton's sonnet line saying that people who merely remain in place patiently are serving too, exactly what a queue does

explanation.surface: People in a line are useful too, as the poet said.
explanation.walkthrough: Milton, On His Blindness: 'They also serve who only stand and wait'. A queue does exactly that.
explanation.definitionFit: Queuers remain on their feet and are patient, the activity the poem names.

clue.text: Corn suffering from a long haul by road

definitions.meaning: a corn is a hard painful patch on the toe

definitions.text: suffering from a long haul by road
definitions.meaning: tired and aching after a long walk

explanation.surface: Grain wearying after a long lorry trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A corn is a painful spot on the toe; long walks leave feet aching.

clue.text: Double serving of mince meat for a sporting pal

indicators.note: minced meat is chopped up, so the letters are rearranged
a double serving gives two portions of the following word

explanation.surface: Two portions of minced meat for a friend from sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double serving of' gives MEATMEAT, which 'mince' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the same side in a game is a fellow player.

clue.text: How the dissolute, erratic seam bowler plays

definitions.text: How the dissolute, erratic seam bowler plays

parts.words: How the dissolute, erratic seam bowler plays
parts.note: an immoral person plays recklessly with rules; a quick bowler who is wild sends the ball quickly and wildly

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler who is quick and wayward, likened to a rake.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a seam bowler is usually a quick one; erratic means wayward. The idiom 'play ... and ...' means to behave irresponsibly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means behaving irresponsibly, and literally describes a quick, wild bowler.

clue.text: A scholar in India's philosophy and in mine

indicators.note: in places one word within the other

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Indian philosophical sage found down a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned Hindu teacher versed in Sanskrit lore, also called a pundit.

clue.text: Praise anew the old Iran

indicators.note: anew means the letters are set out afresh

explanation.surface: Glorifying the ancient land again.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran was formerly known by this name in the West until 1935.

clue.text: Copy the third last letter to a point

parts.note: to ape is to imitate
in the alphabet X comes before Y and Z

explanation.surface: Imitating a letter of the alphabet until reaching a tip.
explanation.definitionFit: The summit or tip of something is its highest point.

clue.text: What an angler takes for a Sunday by the lake

parts.note: a pool is a small body of still water

explanation.surface: A fisherman going out to the water on a Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglers carry a reel on which the line is wound.

clue.text: Object to a newspaper report

definitions.meaning: a single piece of news in a paper

explanation.surface: Protesting at something printed in the press.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a single thing and a short news piece share the same word.

clue.text: It is used in verses from the Lowlands

definitions.text: It is used in verses from the Lowlands

indicators.note: used in shows the letters sit inside the next word

explanation.surface: A tongue employed in poetry from southern Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Lowland Scots called the Gaelic of the Highlands Erse; it sits inside 'verses'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lowland Scots term for Gaelic speech.

clue.text: A gripping description of evil

definitions.meaning: a bench tool with jaws that grips

explanation.surface: An exciting account of wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: A workshop clamp, and also wickedness or depravity.

clue.text: Seize goods from the railroad to hell

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, hell
a train runs on a railroad

explanation.surface: A train to the underworld from which property is confiscated.
explanation.definitionFit: To distrain is the legal term for confiscating property to cover a debt.

clue.text: Maim so unconventional and sensitive a flower

indicators.note: the letters are put in an unconventional order

explanation.surface: Unusually hurting a delicate bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and sensitive a' extends the definition: Mimosa pudica is known as the sensitive plant, folding when touched.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant with fluffy yellow blooms, so a flower by example.

clue.text: Tray containing underwear used for burlesque

indicators.note: containing tells us one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
a vest is an undershirt in British English

explanation.surface: A tray with a vest on it used in a comic stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a vest is an undershirt worn beneath clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A burlesque is a grotesque parody, a synonym for a mockery.

clue.text: Respect always lies at the heart of Religious Education

indicators.note: something lying at the heart of another sits in its middle

parts.note: RE is the school subject's abbreviation
ever means always

explanation.surface: Reverence for eternity is central to RE lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere is to venerate or hold in deep esteem.
